summary: Yes, Random Forest classifier achieves significantly higher stratified 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC (0.9068 ± 0.0019) compared to Logistic Regression (0.8544 ± 0.0030), with a difference of 0.0525. This finding is stable and confirmed across repeated cross-validation with different random seeds.
methodological_choices: Removed rows with missing values (NaN in workclass, occupation, native-country columns), resulting in 48,842 clean samples with 14 features. Encoded 8 categorical variables using LabelEncoder. Applied StandardScaler to features in Logistic Regression pipeline (required for proper model function), but not for Random Forest. Used both models with scikit-learn defaults (RandomForestClassifier and LogisticRegression with random_state=42). Evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with ROC-AUC as the metric. Class distribution was imbalanced (11,687 positive vs 37,155 negative).
verification_method: Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repetitions using different random seeds (RepeatedStratifiedKFold), yielding 50 total folds per model. Compared 95% confidence intervals derived from repeated CV scores to assess finding stability.
verification_result: Finding is CONFIRMED and STABLE. RF maintained higher mean ROC-AUC (0.906988 ± 0.003595) compared to LR (0.854346 ± 0.003781) across repeated CV. Confidence intervals do not overlap: RF 95% CI [0.900616, 0.911969] vs LR 95% CI [0.846918, 0.860889]. The ROC-AUC difference of 0.0525 persisted consistently (original 5-fold: 0.0525, repeated CV: 0.0526).
